The verdict is **fix**: the change itself is sound, but the doc that describes the processes is now out of date. The review is in `deputy/review.md`.

**What the diff does:** it adds an `index` step to the build and design processes. In that step the builder adds a line to the readme of each folder it touched, and links each new page from its parent page. It also makes the build plan show the look first (a Figma frame or a screenshot) before anything more is built. Both changes are in `BuildProcess.js` and `DesignProcess.js`, and the test now expects eight steps instead of seven.

**What must change:**
- `core/Task/doc/process.md` still lists the old steps on lines 5, 69 and 70, without `index`. Rule 9 in CLAUDE.md says a system's docs must match its code, so those lines should be updated on the same branch.

**Worth a look:**
- **It doesn't finish any item in the brief.** At most it covers part of item 4 ("a builder that builds a whole system documents it"). The main part of item 4 is still to do: writing the docs rule into the documentation skill, `ai/doc/readme-system.md` and the mastermind role readme.
- **The step name is safe.** Nothing on Task, Process or Item is called `index`, so the name won't call a method by accident.
- **The design process isn't tested.** The test only covers the build process, so nothing checks the new step in the design process.
- **There's no simpler way.** A separate step is the plainest design. The same step text is written out in both processes; sharing one copy would stop them drifting apart, but that's optional.

There were no screenshots for this diff, so the review covers only the owner's requests and the wording.

**Real pass:** after the merge, the deputy runs `node Server/ProposalTriage.mjs --apply <dir>`. That moves each proposal and writes the manifest `ai/asks/triage.jsonl`. Until then the card on the undone asks page says "No triage has run yet."

**Card tests:** I tested the card at 400 and 1200 px, and pressed Approve all against scratch copies only. The backlog count went from 1 to 0. The screenshots are in `proposals/shots`, but that folder is gitignored, so they are not in the commit. I did not press Approve all on real tasks.

**Review:** passed with six notes and no must-fix. I answered each as a reply to the review (one marked fixed, five no change needed):
- **Priority shape:** `{score: 4-N, big: N}` rather than the plain `priority: N` the brief asked for. `run_item` accepted it on the scratch apply test.
- **Approve all:** it approves the backlog tasks without giving them a priority.
- **Other notes:** no screenshots in the diff, unstyled `triage-*` classes, hard-coded priority names in the card, and the bulk of the Haiku batch data.

I built the review page as a sessions-list variant at `/framework/ai/sessions/v/review/` and stopped there for your look, as asked. Nothing is merged; it's all on branch `worktree/qf-3` at `c5d5a1b85`.

**What the page does:**
- Lists recent sessions, each nested under the session that spawned it. Today's 36 sessions fold under 26 parents; the phone variant finds no parent links for the same day.
- A **Today ▾** pill switches to Week, Month or Year, and the choice stays in the url. Year reads at most 60 days of files for now.
- The head card shows three totals (**approved**, **waiting**, **leaking**) and an **Approve all finished** button.
- Every row has an **Approve** button, a plain title, a line saying what it belongs to ("minion, for …"), and the slug in small type. Approving a parent covers everything under it.
- A **leak** is a session nobody approved that finished over a day ago and cost more than $0.50. Leaks are listed first, in red. On real data the week shows $561 waiting and $1,084 leaking across 139 sessions.
- At 1920 the head card sits beside the list.

**Tested:** I shot it at 400 and 1920, Today and Week. I pressed Approve in a headless browser against the worktree's copy of the data:
- It wrote `{"approve":{"at":"2026-10-24T00:42:04.952Z","by":"owner"}}` to that session's own `session.jsonl`.
- It also added a pointer line to that day's `day.jsonl`.
- The totals moved from $0.00 to $0.78 approved and from 139 to 138 leaks.
- I then moved those test lines aside.

**What the tab shows for this session:**
- **Head:** its plain title, $227.41 of its own cost and $314.01 including everything under it, and how long it ran. It also says "36 of 71 tasks complete", where only tasks whose record says `complete` count. The open tasks are listed by title.
- **Controls:** the Today ▾ pill, three totals ($0.00 approved, $0.71 waiting, $85.88 leaking), and Approve all for the whole session.
- **Rows:** 29 at the top level with 41 more folded inside them, never one flat list. Each row shows its title, its own and rolled-up cost, its duration, "n of m tasks complete" (or "no tasks recorded"), its state and an Approve button. Leaks are red.

**Where the nesting comes from:** I couldn't fix it in the script that writes `session-tree.json`. Servex records the 21 task masterminds as children of your session, but never records the minions they spawned. So no fix to that script can add the missing level. Instead the tab nests by task folder, because each child's record sits inside its parent's folder. The proper fix is for Servex to record the parent when it spawns an agent; that's a Servex change I didn't make.

Your guess was partly right. The causes were:

- **prompts.jsonl (two 404s):** the worktree's `sessions.json` has no row for this agent, so `load_row` returned null and the page read prompts. The page now asks only when `directory.json` lists a `prompts.jsonl` in the session's folder.
- **session-index.json:** `show_role` called `load_index(this.url)`, the session page's own URL. It now passes `this.home.url`.

Fixing those two exposed more errors, and each one made the roles page fail the merge check:

- **Flat-folder fallback:** the roles page links many other agents' session pages, and each of those failed. `AISession.read_text` fell back to probing the old flat folder, which 404s. I removed the fallback. The one remaining flat folder, `a56900e3-8b50-49d0-bb1c-42f986cd407b`, holds only generated files (`cache.jsonl`, `index.json`).
- **Raw link probe:** the "Raw" link did a sync HEAD on `own_dir + "session.jsonl"` while `own_dir` was still a flat path. It now probes only once the dated folder is known.
